summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 20%), COPD, type 2 diabetes, schizophrenia, and substance use was admitted for acute decompensated heart failure following a recent reduction in his torsemide dose from 40 mg to 20 mg. He presented with worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and leg swelling. Evaluation revealed pulmonary edema on chest imaging and elevated proBNP. He was treated with IV furosemide, which improved his symptoms and resolved his hypoxia and edema. His kidney function showed mild acute injury, likely due to over-diuresis, with creatinine rising to 1.4. He was stabilized at his dry weight of 88 kg, transitioned back to oral torsemide 20 mg daily, and had lisinopril reduced to 2.5 mg daily. He denied recent cocaine use, and urine toxicology was negative. He was discharged home with instructions to monitor daily weights, follow a low-sodium diet, and attend follow-up with a heart failure specialist, with outpatient lab monitoring planned.
